title: Close-Grip Bench Press
summary: A bench press with a narrower grip that works the triceps harder.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; rack with J-hooks (power rack, squat stands or bench uprights); flat bench.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for triceps (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly triceps total.
Library rating 0.6 for chest (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly chest total.
Library rating 0.4 for front delts (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly front delts total.

setup.text: Lie on the bench and grip the bar about shoulder width apart.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Press until your arms are straight.

form_cues.cue: Keep elbows tucked close to your sides
Shoulder width is close enough. A grip that's too narrow just strains your wrists.

mistakes.text: Gripping so narrow that the wrists bend back.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where you can fail a rep safely, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.
